Usage: perch [<branch>]       Go to the branch, wherever it lives
       perch br [<branch>]    Check the branch out here
       perch wt [<branch>]    Give the branch its own worktree
       perch wt <name> <branch>
                                  Use a custom worktree directory name

       perch .                Refresh the current branch from its remote
       perch -- <branch>      Go to a branch named br/shell/wt
       perch br rm [<branch>] Remove local branches
       perch wt ls            List worktrees
       perch wt rm [<branch>|.]
       perch shell install    Add the shell integration to your rc file

A <branch> to go to can also be `pr:<n>`, a GitHub pull request, or
`mr:<n>`, a GitLab merge request.

With the shell integration loaded, `br` and `wt` stand in for `perch br`
and `perch wt`. Set PERCH_NO_SHORTCUTS to leave both names alone.
